advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Assert the SSM command reached a Success status (check ResponseCode/StandardErrorContent) before trusting its stdout in probe_host().
evidence: get-command-invocation only queries "--query","StandardOutputContent" and never StatusDetails/ResponseCode
No check that the remote lsblk exited 0; a partial stdout buffer is parsed as authoritative host state
Litmus: the check produces its 'in-service' verdict both when lsblk truly ran and when the probe returned truncated output — the failure of the instrument is invisible
advisory.finding: probe_host() trusts SSM StandardOutputContent without ever checking the remote command's status/ResponseCode. If the lsblk invocation on the host errored or returned truncated output, the assertion parses whatever partial text came back and can misclassify volumes; only the fully-empty case is caught (via UNKNOWN). The probe cannot distinguish 'host reported cleanly' from 'the probe command failed and returned partial output'.
scenarios: SSM command times out mid-execution and returns partial StandardOutputContent
lsblk emits a warning/partial table on an unusual host

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Inspect the `ssm wait` result (or use check=True with handling) so a wait/command failure surfaces instead of being swallowed.
evidence: subprocess.run([... "ssm","wait","command-executed" ...], capture_output=True, text=True, check=False)
The CompletedProcess return value is discarded — returncode is never examined
advisory.finding: The `aws ssm wait command-executed` subprocess uses check=False and its result is neither inspected nor its stderr surfaced. A wait failure (timeout, command Failed/Cancelled, still InProgress) is silently swallowed and execution falls straight through to get-command-invocation.
scenarios: Command still InProgress when wait's internal poll budget expires

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Restrict partition rollup to true partition children (e.g. match a 'p<digits>' suffix) rather than any name prefix.
evidence: mount = next((m for dev, m in sorted(mounts.items()) if dev != name and dev.startswith(name)), None)
Comment scopes intent to 'nvme0n1p1 -> nvme0n1' but the predicate matches any name-prefix, not partition-suffix specifically
advisory.finding: The partition-mount rollup uses `dev.startswith(name)`, which can cross-match unrelated sibling devices whose names share a prefix (e.g. a device named 'nvme1n1' would match 'nvme1n10' or any longer sibling), causing an unmounted device to inherit a sibling's mountpoint and be reported in-service.
scenarios: Two attached block devices where one full name is a string prefix of another
Future device naming schemes without a 'p<N>' partition delimiter
advisory.suggested_fix: Match with a regex like `re.fullmatch(rf'{re.escape(name)}p\d+', dev)` instead of `dev.startswith(name)`.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Detect duplicate normalised serials in parse_host_mounts rather than silently overwriting.
evidence: resolved[serial] = mount  # last-writer-wins over dict iteration order
Serial normalisation `.replace("-","")` strips ALL dashes, widening collision surface beyond the intended single 'vol-' dash
advisory.finding: parse_host_mounts keys the resolved map by serial, so if two block devices report the same (or dash-normalised colliding) SERIAL, the later iteration silently overwrites the earlier mount state with no error.
scenarios: Duplicate/blank-normalised serials in an unexpected lsblk report

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Correct gate-scratch-mount.md §9 to cite the gate_scratch_mounted probe at observability.sh:210-213 (dimensionless) rather than the disk_used_percent df branch at :233/:238.
evidence: infra/runbooks/gate-scratch-mount.md: 'If `gate_scratch_mounted` still reads 0, the metric publisher is `infra/scripts/observability.sh` (`GATE_SCRATCH_MOUNT` default at `:72`, probe at `:233`, dimension at `:238`)'

infra/scripts/observability.sh:210-213: `scratch_mounted=0` / `[ -f "$GATE_SCRATCH_MOUNT/.gate-scratch-mounted" ] && scratch_mounted=1` / `--metric-name gate_scratch_mounted --unit Count` is where gate_scratch_mounted is published
infra/scripts/observability.sh:208: 'DIMENSIONLESS, following root_disk_used_percent (2b) and the dimensionless alarm in monitoring_autodeploy.tf.' contradicts the runbook's 'dimension at :238'

infra/scripts/observability.sh:231-238: lines 233 and 238 belong to the disk_used_percent df branch (`scratch_pct=$(df ...)` and `--metric-name disk_used_percent ... --dimensions ...`), not the gate_scratch_mounted probe
advisory.finding: The gate-scratch-mount.md §9 troubleshooting note misattributes the observability.sh code for the gate_scratch_mounted metric. It tells an operator debugging a 'gate_scratch_mounted still reads 0' condition that the metric publisher is at 'probe at :233, dimension at :238', but line 233 computes scratch_pct via df and line 238 is the --dimensions argument for the disk_used_percent metric, not gate_scratch_mounted. The gate_scratch_mounted probe is at observability.sh:210-213 and is documented as DIMENSIONLESS at :208, so both the probe line and the claim of a dimension are wrong for the metric the sentence is about.
scenarios: An operator sees gate_scratch_mounted=0 after remediation and opens observability.sh at :233 to check the probe, landing on the disk_used_percent df branch instead of the gate_scratch_mounted publisher at :210-213.
advisory.suggested_fix: In gate-scratch-mount.md §9, change the parenthetical to point at the gate_scratch_mounted publisher (observability.sh:210-213, dimensionless per :208); if a disk_used_percent pointer is also wanted, label :231-238 as the disk_used_percent branch separately.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a parse_host_mounts test with a sibling device whose name is a prefix of another (e.g. nvme0n1 vs nvme0n10) to pin that only true partitions roll up.
evidence: scripts/assert_volumes_in_service.py:136: `(m for dev, m in sorted(mounts.items()) if dev != name and dev.startswith(name)),`

The only rollup test, `test_a_volume_mounted_through_its_PARTITION_is_not_reported_unmounted`, uses `nvme0n1`/`nvme0n1p1` where the prefix relation is a true parent/partition; no test uses a sibling like `nvme0n10` whose name also starts with `nvme0n1` but is a distinct device.
ABSENCE: no fixture in REAL_HOST_REPORT or any parametrized case introduces two devices where one name is a prefix of an unrelated other device name.
advisory.finding: The partition-rollup logic added at parse_host_mounts uses `dev.startswith(name)` as the parent/partition test, which matches sibling devices, not only partitions. There is no test exercising a device whose name is a prefix of an unrelated sibling device (e.g. `nvme0n1` and `nvme0n10`, or `nvme1` and `nvme12`), so a wrong sibling's mount could be rolled up to a device, misclassifying an unmounted volume as IN-SERVICE. The added rollup behavior is untested for this collision input.
scenarios: A host enumerates both `nvme0n1` (unmounted attached volume) and `nvme0n10` (a separate mounted device); the rollup rolls nvme0n10's mount up to nvme0n1 and reports the unmounted volume as IN-SERVICE, re-introducing the exact silent-fallback the script exists to catch.
advisory.suggested_fix: Add a test asserting an unmounted `nvme0n1` is NOT credited with `nvme0n10`'s mount, and tighten the rollup match to a partition-shaped suffix (e.g. `dev[len(name):].lstrip('p').isdigit()`) rather than a bare `startswith`.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Anchor the partition rollup to the real partition-suffix form (e.g. dev == name + 'p<N>' or a regex like ^{name}p\d+$) instead of a bare dev.startswith(name).
evidence: `mount = next((m for dev, m in sorted(mounts.items()) if dev != name and dev.startswith(name)), None,)`
Comment claims 'Roll a partition's mount up to its parent device: nvme0n1p1 -> nvme0n1.' but startswith is not restricted to the `<name>p<N>` partition suffix form
advisory.finding: parse_host_mounts rolls a partition mount up to its parent via `dev.startswith(name)`, an unanchored prefix match that can mis-attribute a mount to the wrong device — e.g. an unmounted device named as a prefix of another mounted device (nvme1 vs nvme1n1, or nvme0n1 vs a hypothetical nvme0n10) — producing a false IN-SERVICE verdict for a genuinely unmounted attached volume.
advisory.suggested_fix: Replace `dev.startswith(name)` with a partition-suffix match, e.g. `re.fullmatch(re.escape(name) + r'p\d+', dev)`.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Check the SSM invocation Status/ResponseCode in probe_host and raise a distinct error when the probe itself failed, rather than treating empty stdout as an absent device.
evidence: `aws ssm wait command-executed ... check=False`
`--query`, `StandardOutputContent` — only stdout is read; no ResponseCode/Status check
A failed probe returns empty stdout, which parse_host_mounts turns into {} and classify maps to UNKNOWN
advisory.finding: probe_host does not verify the SSM command succeeded on the host: `aws ssm wait` is invoked with check=False and get-command-invocation unconditionally reads StandardOutputContent, ignoring the invocation Status/ResponseCode.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Wire assert_volumes_in_service.py into an enforced post-apply step (Terraform check block / CI job / scheduled run) so a newly-attached-but-unmounted volume fails automatically rather than by operator memory.
evidence: Docstring: 'It is an operation-linked check -- run it after an apply, from a runbook, or from any scheduler -- and it is not wired to any one CI provider.'
gate-scratch-mount.md §10: 'Run it after this procedure, and after ANY future `terraform apply` that adds or replaces a volume'
ABSENCE: no Terraform check/postcondition, provisioner, or CI wiring in the diff invokes assert_volumes_in_service.py automatically
advisory.finding: The attached-vs-in-service drift check is advisory/operation-linked only — it is not wired into `terraform apply` or any enforced gate — so the structural gap it closes (a volume attached after first boot never entering service) still relies on an operator remembering to run the script after every apply.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Document the minimal IAM permissions (scoped ssm:SendCommand/GetCommandInvocation on the target instance and AWS-RunShellScript document) needed to run the probe.
evidence: probe_host calls `aws ssm send-command --document-name AWS-RunShellScript`, `aws ssm wait command-executed`, `aws ssm get-command-invocation`
ABSENCE: no statement of the required IAM actions/resource scoping in the docstring or gate-scratch-mount.md §10 which invokes the script
advisory.finding: Neither the script docstring nor the runbook documents the least-privilege IAM permissions the SSM-based probe requires (ssm:SendCommand on AWS-RunShellScript, ssm:GetCommandInvocation, and the target-instance scoping), leaving the operator/runner's grant unspecified.
